cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll work out why nobody reached the meeting. I moved it to three. What happened to the room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved it without telling me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Put that under my name. I'll send the correction once you've told me where you sent everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First tell me why you didn't warn me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I thought you'd veto three. I'll put that in the message too. Which room do I need to apologise for?

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unannounced-change challenge causes A3 public ownership; B4 why-question causes A5 actual veto motive and renewed room query.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 seek accountability before cooperating, rather than conceding on cue.

heightening.evidence: A5 increases A exposure to make B room detail the remaining gap in the apology.

specificity.evidence: A1 failed meeting, changed time and room question give coherent missing components.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 motive, public inclusion and one question each have a specific purpose in eliciting B disclosure.
